entities.summary: Ka‛ ibn Zuhayr was an Arabian poet of the 7th century, and a contemporary of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. He was born in Mecca, Arabia, and rose to prominence as a major poet and intellectual figure in the early Islamic era. His poetry, which often dealt with themes of love, spirituality, and social justice, was widely admired and studied by his contemporaries. Ibn Zuhayr's work had a significant impact on the development of Arabic literature, and his influence can still be seen in the poetry of later Arab and Islamic writers. He is often regarded as one of the greatest poets of the pre-Islamic era, and his legacy continues to be celebrated in the Arab world. Ibn Zuhayr's poetry is characterized by its musical quality, its use of metaphor and imagery, and its exploration of themes that were central to Islamic thought, such as the nature of God and the human condition. He was a key figure in the development of Arabic poetry, and his work helped to shape the literary style and themes of the Islamic Golden Age. Ibn Zuhayr's legacy extends beyond the world of literature, as his poetry and intellectual ideas also influenced the development of Islamic theology and philosophy. His work continues to be studied and admired by scholars and readers around the world.
